headline: Finland's wireless and electronics sector is strong on 6G and AI-driven network demand, while the EU's Chips Act 2.0 and the January 2027 6G call are still pending.
outlook_reason: Nokia sales are growing on AI and cloud demand, the EU and Business Finland are putting money into 6G, chips and photonics, and Finnish deep-tech startups keep closing rounds, though Chips Act 2.0 is still undecided.

signals.title: Business Finland launches growth projects for space, semiconductors and photonics, and AI in manufacturing
signals.detail: The semiconductor and photonics project is a coordination and market-access vehicle: it helps firms find partners, join EU cooperation and reach pilot lines. It is not a direct funding award, and no budget was stated.

signals.title: Nokia Q3 2026 results
signals.detail: Net sales were €5,154M (+10%). AI and cloud customer sales rose 123%, IP Networks 43% and Optical 18%. Operating profit outlook for 2026 is €2.1–2.6B. The date is the report date, not checked against the release page.

signals.title: SNS JU funds five 6G projects worth about €22M
signals.detail: The projects turn 6G research into industrial innovation. A further call of about €220M is reported for January 2027. The exact publication date was not checked, so this date is approximate.

signals.title: Chips Act 2.0 still in early negotiation
signals.detail: The Council held a policy debate at the Competitiveness Council; one source says 24 September, another 24 October. Member States are divided on budget, technology priorities, EU preference and advanced manufacturing. ITRE reportedly named MEP Oliver Schenk as rapporteur. No Council general approach or Parliament position was found. The date is approximate.

signals.title: Nokia expands 6G and defence network R&D in Finland with Business Finland support
signals.detail: Reported in search results and not checked on the page (the Nokia page returned an error). Amount unknown. This is older than 30 days and is kept from the search results for context.
